title: Dataset Selection Rationale for Multi-Modal SCIM Fault Detection
motivation: No single public benchmark provides synchronised multi-modal data (vibration + current + thermal + RUL) from a single squirrel-cage induction motor (SCIM) under controlled fault conditions. Dataset selection was therefore guided by fault-type coverage, SCIM applicability, and data availability. This limitation motivates the Latent Digital Twin approach.

available_datasets_considered.name: CWRU Bearing Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: High — induction motor bearings at 1750 RPM
available_datasets_considered.reason: Gold standard for bearing fault classification; 4 fault types; 12kHz sampling; widely benchmarked

available_datasets_considered.name: NASA IMS Bearing Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: High — run-to-failure bearing data enabling RUL regression
available_datasets_considered.reason: Only public bearing dataset with complete run-to-failure RUL labels; enables Bi-LSTM-Attn training

available_datasets_considered.name: Induction Motor Current Signature Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: Very High — data captured directly from SCIM under motor fault conditions
available_datasets_considered.reason: SCIM-specific vibration with 4 fault classes; temporal degradation provides realistic training data

available_datasets_considered.name: Motor Current Signature Analysis (3-Phase)
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: Very High — 3-phase current directly measures stator/rotor faults in SCIM
available_datasets_considered.reason: Only public 3-phase current dataset with SCIM fault labels; enables Current-CNN expert model

available_datasets_considered.name: Thermal Camera Motor Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: High — IR thermography is standard industrial motor health monitoring
available_datasets_considered.reason: Covers thermal modality not present in other benchmark datasets; enables early thermal fault detection

available_datasets_considered.name: FEMTO / PRONOSTIA Bearing Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: Medium — test rig bearings not directly from SCIM; different failure modes
available_datasets_considered.reason_not_selected: Already covered by IMS for RUL; test rig bearings differ from SCIM motor bearings; no stator/rotor fault data

available_datasets_considered.name: MFPT Bearing Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: Medium — general bearing faults, not SCIM-specific
available_datasets_considered.reason_not_selected: Subset of fault types covered by CWRU; no additional modalities or fault types

available_datasets_considered.name: Paderborn University Bearing Dataset
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: Medium — test rig data; includes motor current but at test rig level not SCIM
available_datasets_considered.reason_not_selected: Current modality covered by dedicated MCSA dataset with SCIM-specific faults (BRB); Paderborn lacks rotor fault data critical for SCIM diagnosis

available_datasets_considered.name: MIMII Dataset (Malfunctioning Industrial Machine)
available_datasets_considered.scim_applicability: Low — acoustic anomaly detection, not SCIM-specific fault classification
available_datasets_considered.reason_not_selected: Acoustic modality not in scope; no fault-class labels for specific SCIM failure modes

conclusion: The five selected datasets collectively cover all four target modalities (vibration, 3-phase current, thermal, RUL) with SCIM-specific fault types (bearing faults, broken rotor bars, stator winding faults, thermal degradation). No single dataset covers all modalities simultaneously — this fundamental data scarcity in the SCIM PHM domain is the primary motivation for the Latent Digital Twin approach, which generates physics-consistent co-located multi-modal training data.
